newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Long bonds ended slightly weaker on Wednesday after an initial attempt to extend the market's two-day rally was thwarted by profit-taking, dealers said.
At 1420 GMT, the key R150 was pegged at a 14.795 percent yield after it settled at 14.775 percent overnight. The R150 began the week at 14.96 percent.
The market initially probed the 14.70 level after gains on the U.S. Treasury bond market overnight triggered early local jobber and institutional demand.
"This morning we started chasing the U.S. but it died down and profit-taking set in," a dealer said, adding: "There was a big jobber level at 14.70 percent."
Dealers said that after the initial rally, the market slowly drifted higher for the rest of the day, meeting insufficient demand on the way up to counter the move.
Even a slightly better-than-expected March consumer inflation number did little to enthuse the market.

The Central Statistical Service reported that the consumer price index rose 0.6 percent month-on-month and 9.6 percent year-on-year in March. That compared with a market consensus forecast of a 0.7 and 9.7 percent increase.
"The CPI was pretty much in line with expectations and the market did not react to it," a trader said.
Dealers said that in the absence of any further pointers, the market was now looking to the release of March money supply and private sector credit extension data at 1500 GMT on Friday for direction.
Technically, however, the market still looked strong, having broken a number of long-term moving averages and other technical levels on its way down this week.
But dealers said that with market holidays coming up next Monday and Thursday and options close-out next Friday, they expected the market to consolidate around current levels in the short-term.
R150 was expected to move in a 14.82 to 14.76 percent range in the short-term.
Bond Exchange figures show foreigners were net buyers of 577.02 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after buying 182.85 million on Monday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at a healthy 8.8 billion rand from 3.15 billion previously.
On the currency market, the rand was confined to a tight 4.44 to 4.4450 bid range on the day as good importer demand neutralised bond investment-related offshore dollar inflows.
The rand was last quoted at 4.4445/4475 against the U.S. currency from 4.4465/4485 overnight.
"Its been pretty much the same as the last couple of days," a dealer said, "not much happening and a very tight range."
Dealers said the rand's attempt to move below the 4.44 level was stymied by substantial importer interest to buy dollars, while dollars were in healthy supply at around the 4.4475 level.

"A lot of dollars are coming in from offshore...it looks like its related to bond investments," a dealer said, adding that local banks had also been selling dollars on the day "on improved sentiment".

The fact that the currency had bounced off the 4.44 level on the day meant that a technical base had begun to form there, which dealers said signalled the rand would find it difficult to break below that level.
On the topside, however, they said that 4.45 looked toppish in the short-term.
Against the crosses, the rand was last trading at 28.3485/3901 yen from 28.3473/3889 on Tuesday, at 0.3854/3858 marks from 0.3846/3850 and at 7.2188/2281 against sterling from 7.2727/2820 overnight.
As expected, South Africa's money market shortage moved back above the seven billion rand mark after falling to a six month-low on Monday.
The Reserve Bank pegged the shortage at 7.344 billion rand on Tuesday from 6.743 billion rand.
Major banks kept their three month deposit rates steady at between 16.40 to 16.45 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at between 15.80 to 16.00 percent.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
